title: setDesiredAPY commit is mempool-visible: stakers can front-run the commit to lock in a higher (or lower) accPhUSDPerShare than the protocol intends
rootCause: The two-step gate is economically useless against front-runners: the committed value equals the public `pendingAPYBps`, so a sophisticated staker can stake right before commit (debt-anchored at OLD acc) and benefit from the NEW rate immediately after. Conversely, a front-runner can claim before a downward commit to lock in the higher OLD rate.

symbolic.claim: The two-step gate state machine is correctly implemented — which is precisely why this finding is interesting: the gate works exactly as advertised, and 'as advertised' provides no MEV protection.

impactSummary: Two-step gate is economically useless against the very actors it should slow down. Honest passive stakers do not benefit; active mempool-watching stakers and bots capture the rate-change delta.
preservedDetails: ECON-004 carries the strongest economic framing of the MEV failure. Distinct from DEDUP-016 (CODE-010 / state-cleanup spec gap) because the angle differs: CODE-010 is about misleading view-state after commit, ECON-004 is about the gate's design intent failing against MEV.
remediation: Use private mempool for commit tx; longer time-based window; rate-change cooldown on new stakes; time-weighted accrual.
dedupNotes: Shares the setDesiredAPY surface with DEDUP-006 (uncapped magnitude) and DEDUP-016 (CODE-010 stale pending state). Three distinct findings on the same function: magnitude (DEDUP-006), MEV-around-legitimate-changes (DEDUP-010), and state-hygiene-after-commit (DEDUP-016). Kept separate because remediations and stakeholder harms differ.
